sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A well-prepared bachelor-level applicant can apply; mathematics major not strictly necessary. Department
looks for undergraduate breadth including analysis/algebra, some depth, research potential, motivation and
faculty fit. UChicago math degree is appropriate preparation in form; degree must be awarded before
matriculation. [s1] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics doctoral program, not Applied Mathematics. Prepare transcripts, three referees, SOP,
supplemental essay and new short mathematical video. Verify portal-only video specifications before
recording. Request need-based fee waiver in application early if needed. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement listed; interests should fit faculty. Current regular faculty below; temporary
Tamarkin/postdoctoral appointments and emeriti not treated as ordinary long-term primary-advisor options.

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL or IELTS when not exempt. TOEFL minimum 90 for tests before 21 January 2026; 4.5 on new scale
thereafter. IELTS recommended overall 7. TOEFL Special Home Edition and IELTS Indicator listed as accepted.
ETS code 3094; IELTS sent electronically to Brown Graduate School, not student-uploaded unofficial report. [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed UChicago degree qualifies under U.S./English-medium degree exemption. Mathematics additionally
exempts applicants already having one or more years of study in an English-speaking country, so a current
UChicago student may qualify before conferral. Central wording emphasizes earned degree; check automatic
waived status 3-5 business days after submission and email admissions after submission if needed.
Native-language-non-English TAs still face arrival certification; lack of certification can affect TA support
beyond first year. [s1] [s4] [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required; public wording does not establish whether a voluntarily supplied score is evaluated, ignored or
blocked. [s1] [s11]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Latest opened central table is FY 2025-26: USD 52,198 gross/12 months = two USD 19,574.25 fall/spring terms
plus USD 13,049.50 summer; monthly USD 4,349.83. This is NOT a 2027-28 offer or verified 2026-27 rate.
Standard package includes tuition remission, health-services fee and insurance; newer admitted-student page
includes health/dental/vision. 2026 incoming cohort received USD 1,750 one-time supplemental fellowship, not
confirmed for 2027. [s8] [s9] [s16] [s17]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math promises five years; first year fellowship without teaching, later usually TA/Teaching Fellow. Department
tries for another nonteaching semester. Summer stipend available for study/research toward PhD; summer
teaching opportunities also exist. Sixth year case by case. Central “five or six years” language does not
override Math’s five-year statement. [s7] [s17]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
All doctoral admits covered by central support guarantee without nationality exception; inference: international
Math admits included. External awards/loans may have citizenship restrictions. [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Satisfactory progress, full-time residential dedication, annual appointments. Summer support tied to PhD
study/research. Later teaching requires English certification for nonnative speakers; after first year uncertified
students cannot remain supported as TAs. [s7] [s8] [s4]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No extra scholarship essay/reference or separate application established for standard Math support; support
comes with admission. External funding rules vary. [s7] [s9]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
External fellowships and university incentive/support programs; sixth-year/dissertation-extension requests
through program. Individual eligibility and deadlines distinct. External paid training up to 12 hours/week is a
university academic rule, not immigration work authorization. [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75 nonrefundable, due with application; no refund for applicant error. [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Needs-based request in Additional Information with short hardship explanation and ONLY listed evidence:
current/recent financial-aid package, FAFSA/CSS showing EFC, unemployment verification within 90 days,
GRE/TOEFL reduction voucher. Submit with waiver request at least two weeks before deadline recommended
(18 December 2026 calculated); notice on submission. Provisional waiver can be denied after document review
and application revert to unsubmitted until payment. No late waiver requests/payment deferral. International
F-1 status alone is not a waiver basis. [s5] [s10]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A well-prepared bachelor-level applicant can apply; mathematics major not strictly necessary. Department
looks for undergraduate breadth including analysis/algebra, some depth, research potential, motivation and
faculty fit. UChicago math degree is appropriate preparation in form; degree must be awarded before
matriculation. [s1] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics doctoral program, not Applied Mathematics. Prepare transcripts, three referees, SOP,
supplemental essay and new short mathematical video. Verify portal-only video specifications before
recording. Request need-based fee waiver in application early if needed. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement listed; interests should fit faculty. Current regular faculty below; temporary
Tamarkin/postdoctoral appointments and emeriti not treated as ordinary long-term primary-advisor options.

pages. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6]

signatory list. [s14]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL or IELTS when not exempt. TOEFL minimum 90 for tests before 21 January 2026; 4.5 on new scale
thereafter. IELTS recommended overall 7. TOEFL Special Home Edition and IELTS Indicator listed as accepted.
ETS code 3094; IELTS sent electronically to Brown Graduate School, not student-uploaded unofficial report. [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed UChicago degree qualifies under U.S./English-medium degree exemption. Mathematics additionally
exempts applicants already having one or more years of study in an English-speaking country, so a current
UChicago student may qualify before conferral. Central wording emphasizes earned degree; check automatic
waived status 3-5 business days after submission and email admissions after submission if needed.
Native-language-non-English TAs still face arrival certification; lack of certification can affect TA support
beyond first year. [s1] [s4] [s3]

Not required; public wording does not establish whether a voluntarily supplied score is evaluated, ignored or
blocked. [s1] [s11]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]

Unofficial scanned transcripts permitted, with applicant and institution names; include academic
courses/grades. Final official degree transcript required before matriculation. International transcripts need
certified English translation plus original. If security prevents upload, email central admissions after submitting.
Do not convert non-U.S. GPA to 4.0. [s3] [s6] [s10]

Three online letters, at least two from faculty at current or most recently attended institution. Referees should
assess research and graduate-course potential from first-hand knowledge. Interfolio not accepted. [s6]

Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Latest opened central table is FY 2025-26: USD 52,198 gross/12 months = two USD 19,574.25 fall/spring terms

confirmed for 2027. [s8] [s9] [s16] [s17]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math promises five years; first year fellowship without teaching, later usually TA/Teaching Fellow. Department
tries for another nonteaching semester. Summer stipend available for study/research toward PhD; summer
teaching opportunities also exist. Sixth year case by case. Central “five or six years” language does not
override Math’s five-year statement. [s7] [s17]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
All doctoral admits covered by central support guarantee without nationality exception; inference: international
Math admits included. External awards/loans may have citizenship restrictions. [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Satisfactory progress, full-time residential dedication, annual appointments. Summer support tied to PhD
study/research. Later teaching requires English certification for nonnative speakers; after first year uncertified
students cannot remain supported as TAs. [s7] [s8] [s4]

No extra scholarship essay/reference or separate application established for standard Math support; support
comes with admission. External funding rules vary. [s7] [s9]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
External fellowships and university incentive/support programs; sixth-year/dissertation-extension requests
through program. Individual eligibility and deadlines distinct. External paid training up to 12 hours/week is a
university academic rule, not immigration work authorization. [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75 nonrefundable, due with application; no refund for applicant error. [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Needs-based request in Additional Information with short hardship explanation and ONLY listed evidence:
current/recent financial-aid package, FAFSA/CSS showing EFC, unemployment verification within 90 days,
GRE/TOEFL reduction voucher. Submit with waiver request at least two weeks before deadline recommended
(18 December 2026 calculated); notice on submission. Provisional waiver can be denied after document review
and application revert to unsubmitted until payment. No late waiver requests/payment deferral. International
F-1 status alone is not a waiver basis. [s5] [s10]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A well-prepared bachelor-level applicant can apply; mathematics major not strictly necessary. Department
looks for undergraduate breadth including analysis/algebra, some depth, research potential, motivation and
faculty fit. UChicago math degree is appropriate preparation in form; degree must be awarded before
matriculation. [s1] [s6]

Select Mathematics doctoral program, not Applied Mathematics. Prepare transcripts, three referees, SOP,
supplemental essay and new short mathematical video. Verify portal-only video specifications before
recording. Request need-based fee waiver in application early if needed. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5] [s6]

Tamarkin/postdoctoral appointments and emeriti not treated as ordinary long-term primary-advisor options.

English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL or IELTS when not exempt. TOEFL minimum 90 for tests before 21 January 2026; 4.5 on new scale
thereafter. IELTS recommended overall 7. TOEFL Special Home Edition and IELTS Indicator listed as accepted.
ETS code 3094; IELTS sent electronically to Brown Graduate School, not student-uploaded unofficial report. [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed UChicago degree qualifies under U.S./English-medium degree exemption. Mathematics additionally
exempts applicants already having one or more years of study in an English-speaking country, so a current
UChicago student may qualify before conferral. Central wording emphasizes earned degree; check automatic
waived status 3-5 business days after submission and email admissions after submission if needed.
Native-language-non-English TAs still face arrival certification; lack of certification can affect TA support
beyond first year. [s1] [s4] [s3]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Latest opened central table is FY 2025-26: USD 52,198 gross/12 months = two USD 19,574.25 fall/spring terms
plus USD 13,049.50 summer; monthly USD 4,349.83. This is NOT a 2027-28 offer or verified 2026-27 rate.

includes health/dental/vision. 2026 incoming cohort received USD 1,750 one-time supplemental fellowship, not
confirmed for 2027. [s8] [s9] [s16] [s17]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math promises five years; first year fellowship without teaching, later usually TA/Teaching Fellow. Department
tries for another nonteaching semester. Summer stipend available for study/research toward PhD; summer
teaching opportunities also exist. Sixth year case by case. Central “five or six years” language does not
override Math’s five-year statement. [s7] [s17]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
All doctoral admits covered by central support guarantee without nationality exception; inference: international
Math admits included. External awards/loans may have citizenship restrictions. [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Satisfactory progress, full-time residential dedication, annual appointments. Summer support tied to PhD
study/research. Later teaching requires English certification for nonnative speakers; after first year uncertified
students cannot remain supported as TAs. [s7] [s8] [s4]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No extra scholarship essay/reference or separate application established for standard Math support; support
comes with admission. External funding rules vary. [s7] [s9]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
External fellowships and university incentive/support programs; sixth-year/dissertation-extension requests
through program. Individual eligibility and deadlines distinct. External paid training up to 12 hours/week is a
university academic rule, not immigration work authorization. [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75 nonrefundable, due with application; no refund for applicant error. [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Needs-based request in Additional Information with short hardship explanation and ONLY listed evidence:
current/recent financial-aid package, FAFSA/CSS showing EFC, unemployment verification within 90 days,
GRE/TOEFL reduction voucher. Submit with waiver request at least two weeks before deadline recommended
(18 December 2026 calculated); notice on submission. Provisional waiver can be denied after document review
and application revert to unsubmitted until payment. No late waiver requests/payment deferral. International
F-1 status alone is not a waiver basis. [s5] [s10]
